pr.title: Migrate memory overlap check from validator to lint
pr.description:
The check attempts to identify potential undefined behaviour, rather
than whether MIR is well-formed. It belongs in the lint not validator.

Follow up to changes from #119077.
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: No source-grounded runtime counterexample can be constructed for this PR. Its semantic change is a compiler classification move: the memory-overlap check changes from a MIR validator (ill-formedness, all blocks) to a MIR lint (potential UB, reachable blocks only), and DestinationPropagation stops calling remove_dead_blocks after merges. Both the removed dead blocks and the overlap introduced by merging are, by construction, in blocks unreachable from START_BLOCK, so no concrete execution can reach them or observe different values. The deleted regression test `tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/unreachable.rs` only checks MIR dumps: `f` returns `()`, `g` is a no-op, and the before/after diffs differ solely in dead-block removal (bb1 dropped, block indices renumbered); the old and new MIR execute identically for every input. The added `assignment-overlap.rs` and `call-overlap.rs` tests are compile-fail tests (failure-status 101, expected lint/validator diagnostics), not runtime value tests, and overlapping memory in reachable code remains diagnosed in both designs. Constructing two functions that print different values would therefore require either encoding "compiler rejected this program" as an arbitrary sentinel return value or changing reachable computation beyond what the PR's rewrite does, which the instructions forbid. Hence I am not fabricating an unrelated value-difference pair.

analysis.originalLogic: The validator treated certain overlapping-memory patterns as MIR ill-formedness in every block: `Assign` where the destination place equals the `Copy`/`Move` source, and `Call` terminators whose destination place or `Move` arguments duplicate a place. Because `DestinationPropagation` can merge locals and thereby introduce such overlap in unreachable blocks, it compensated by deleting dead blocks: `if round_count != 0 { // Merging can introduce overlap between moved arguments and/or call destination in an unreachable code, which validator considers to be ill-formed. remove_dead_blocks(body); }`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect classification/transformation was to apply the overlap well-formedness rule uniformly to all blocks and to remove unreachable blocks after `DestinationPropagation` solely so the validator would not reject overlap introduced there. The PR reclassifies overlap as potential UB and moves the checks into the MIR lint: `The check attempts to identify potential undefined behaviour, rather than whether MIR is well-formed. It belongs in the lint not validator.` The corrected behavior visits only reachable blocks in the lint and removes the `remove_dead_blocks(body)` cleanup from `DestinationPropagation`, so overlap in unreachable code is not treated as ill-formed and does not force dead-block deletion.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies, especially after local merging by `DestinationPropagation`, containing unreachable blocks with `Assign(dest = copy/move src)` where `dest == src`, or `Call` terminators where the destination place aliases a `Move` argument or two `Move` arguments use the same place. This includes functions where one branch is statically unreachable (for example an `if false` branch) while containing calls such as `g(_1, _1)` after merged locals.
analysis.summary: Historical PR migrates the MIR memory-overlap check from validator (well-formedness) to lint (potential UB), so unreachable overlap is no longer ill-formed. Consequently DestinationPropagation no longer needs to remove dead blocks after merging locals. The patch also fixes validation/linting of injected MIR by reevaluating `body.should_skip()` after MIR phase changes.
analysis.trigger: After `DestinationPropagation` performs at least one merge (`round_count != 0`), merged locals can cause a `Call` destination or multiple `Move` arguments in unreachable code to refer to the same place. Historically this triggered the validator's overlap rejection, so the pass removed dead blocks. With the corrected design, overlap is checked by the reachable-only lint and does not require dead-block removal.
preconditions: The overlapping assignment or call is in an unreachable block, or the lint only visits reachable blocks.
`DestinationPropagation` has merged locals such that call destinations and/or `Move` arguments alias.
`-Zlint-mir` is enabled for the lint check; validator behavior is no longer responsible for this UB check.
Custom MIR tests must use a dialect/phase and unwind action that are well-formed for the injected MIR phase.
pitfalls: Do not treat overlapping memory in an unreachable block as MIR ill-formedness; the check is a potential-UB lint, and the lint visits only reachable blocks.

Do not assume `DestinationPropagation` must delete dead blocks when it introduces overlap in unreachable code; the historical `remove_dead_blocks` call was compensating for validator classification and was removed.
The lint itself notes that it assumes all code can be executed and therefore has false positives; the reachability traversal is the mechanism used here to limit the check.

For injected/custom MIR tests, changing only the phase is insufficient if the test still contains actions forbidden in that phase; the patch changed `#[custom_mir(dialect = "analysis", phase = "post-cleanup")]` to `#[custom_mir(dialect = "runtime")]` and `UnwindContinue()` to `UnwindUnreachable()` in affected tests.

The deleted `tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/unreachable.rs` regression test was specifically about dead-block removal after destination propagation; its deletion does not by itself demonstrate a changed optimization result, because the memory-overlap rule moved out of the validator.
analysis.testStrategy: Use custom MIR UI tests with `// compile-flags: --crate-type=lib -Zlint-mir -Ztreat-err-as-bug`, `// build-fail`, `// failure-status: 101`, and `// dont-check-compiler-stderr`, matching the added error patterns `encountered `Assign` statement with overlapping memory` and `encountered overlapping memory in `Move` arguments to `Call``. Construct two MIR bodies differing only in whether the overlapping code is in a reachable or unreachable block: only the reachable variant should trigger the lint. For `DestinationPropagation`, construct a function with a statically unreachable branch whose calls become overlapping after local merging, run the pass, and verify that surviving MIR may retain the unreachable overlap without validator failure and without requiring forced dead-block removal. Keep custom MIR fixtures phase-valid and use runtime dialect with appropriate unwind actions.
evidence: The check attempts to identify potential undefined behaviour
// Merging can introduce overlap between moved arguments and/or call destination in an
// unreachable code, which validator considers to be ill-formed.
This pass statically detects code which has undefined behaviour or is likely to be erroneous.
It can be used to locate problems in MIR building or optimizations.
// The call destination place and Operand::Move place used as an argument might be
// passed by a reference to the callee. Consequently they must be non-overlapping.
// error-pattern: encountered `Assign` statement with overlapping memory
// error-pattern: encountered overlapping memory in `Move` arguments to `Call`
Reevaluate `body.should_skip()` after updating the MIR phase to ensure
that injected MIR is processed correctly.
